subject: BioHealth: proposed contract buyout & escalated remedies request
messages:
From: Bradley Chen <brad.chen@biohealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@biohealth.ai>, BioHealth Legal <legal@biohealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Buyer request: contractual buyout and fee-hold for uptime misses

Karthik —

Thanks for the demo last week. We like Redwood's performance profile, but two items are blockers for our procurement/legal team before we can recommend a PO:

1) In addition to credits, BioHealth requires an explicit contractual right to exit (buyout) if production SLOs for latency/availability are missed repeatedly during the first 90 days.
2) Our legal team wants 5–10% of the committed first-year fees put into an escrow or fee-hold that can be clawed back as liquidated damages if SLA failures materially impact our operations (we operate regulated clinical workflows).

Credits only are not sufficient for us — we need a combination of a time-bound termination right + a fee at risk to satisfy our board and auditors. We can share sample language.

Please let us know whether Redwood can accept these remedies as a condition of proceeding and, if not, what mitigations you can offer (e.g., enhanced measurement/telemetry, higher SLO tier, extended onboarding support).

Attached initial SLO matrix from our ops team for reference.

Thanks,
Brad Chen
Head of Platform, BioHealth AI
brad.chen@biohealth.ai
+1 415-555-0123

[attachment: biohealth_slo_matrix.xlsx]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Bradley Chen <brad.chen@biohealth.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Buyer request: contractual buyout and fee-hold for uptime misses

Brad —

Appreciate the clarity and the SLO matrix. Short answer: we understand why your auditors want a fee at risk and why a termination right would be attractive — particularly for regulated workloads. We have to run a few legal and risk checks, but we can propose a pragmatic alternative that satisfies auditors while keeping both parties protected.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal alignment with Legal & Risk (I’m looping in Lauren and Priyom).
- We’ll send a targeted counterproposal with clear measurement windows, a staged fee-hold approach, and termination triggers (including cure periods).
- 30‑minute call to align on concrete language this week? I can do 2pm ET Thursday.

We typically avoid open-ended liquidated damages, but we can offer an escrowed holdback + objective thresholds for termination after repeat Severity-1 events. Also happy to include an extended onboarding SLA and joint monitoring access during the first 90 days.

I’ll follow up with a written redline for your counsel.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

[attachment: initial_proposal.docx]

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@biohealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Brad Chen <brad.chen@biohealth.ai>, BioHealth Legal <legal@biohealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 08:25:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Buyer request: contractual buyout and fee-hold for uptime misses

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick response. Legal is explicit: the escrow must be contractually enforceable and release rules must be codified (we usually do monthly release based on SLO attainment). Termination needs to be available after two unremediated S1s in a 90-day window or equivalent sustained degradation.

If Redwood cannot accept that exact structure, we need to understand what concrete mitigations you will give — e.g., double SLO targets for first 60 days, a dedicated 24/7 support line, and an automatic refund formula tied to measured downtime.

Happy to discuss on Thursday.

—Maya
Director, Ops — BioHealth AI
maya.patel@biohealth.ai

[no attachment]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 09:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal: BioHealth escalation — negotiation strategy

Team —

Quick thoughts after reading Brad/Maya:
- Legal will push for hard remedies; we should avoid open-ended liquidated damages unless we can quantify exposure.
- Suggest a staged fee-hold (3% at launch, increase to 5% if SLO breaches continue) with predefined release windows (monthly releases tied to measured SLOs). This meets their auditor needs but limits our cash exposure.
- For termination, offer a right to terminate only after two S1 incidents in a 90-day window AND a 30‑day written cure period following the second S1. That balances their risk tolerance and gives us time to remediate.
- Offer stronger onboarding support (two-week dedicated integration squad + 24/7 escalation for first 60 days) to reduce likelihood of early incidents.

Priyom — can you draft the redline language for the fee-hold + cure window? I’ll review and we can send it to Brad with a clear explanation of the trade-offs.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

[attachment: redlines_for_biohealth_20270811.pdf]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Bradley Chen <brad.chen@biohealth.ai>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@biohealth.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 10:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Buyer request: contractual buyout and fee-hold for uptime misses

Brad/Maya —

Thanks for your patience. Attached is a concise counterproposal based on our legal review (highlights below):

- Fee-hold: 3% of first-year committed fees placed into an escrow. Monthly release: 50% release after each 30-day measurement window where SLOs are met; remainder released at end of 90 days if no recurring breaches. If repeated breaches occur, funds are available per the defined remediation/claims process.
- Termination right: BioHealth may terminate for convenience following two certified Severity-1 incidents in a rolling 90-day window, but Redwood is afforded a 30‑day cure period after the second incident to remediate. Termination would be subject to a pro‑rata refund of unused prepaid fees, minus any amounts properly claimed from escrow per the claims process.
- Measurement: We’ll provide daily SLO dashboards and grant read-only telemetry access to your ops team for the first 90 days. Measurement methodology is in the attachment.

We prefer the staged escrow + cure period because it reduces the need for broad liquidated damages language while giving you auditable protections. If your counsel insists on a larger initial hold, we can discuss increasing the percentage after go‑live triggers.

I’m available 2pm ET Thursday if you want to finalize language.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

[attachment: redlines_for_biohealth_20270811.pdf]

From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@biohealth.ai>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Brad Chen <brad.chen@biohealth.ai>, BioHealth Legal <legal@biohealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Buyer request: contractual buyout & fee-hold for uptime misses

Karthik —

This is helpful and, in principle, moves us forward. A few follow-ups from legal/ops:
- Can you shorten the escrow release cadence to 60%/30%/10% over 30/60/90 days instead of 50%/50%? Our auditors prefer faster partial release.
- We need clarity on the claims process for escrowed funds (who certifies an S1, dispute window, and timeline for payout).
- Confirm that telemetry access includes raw event logs (redacted for PII) and that logs are retained for 180 days.

If you can accept those three tweaks, we will ask legal to run the redline through and sign. Please also fill and return the attached security questionnaire so our InfoSec team can close the final control review.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

—Maya
Director, Ops — BioHealth AI
maya.patel@biohealth.ai
